issues.legal_issue: A land does not cease to be vacant land merely because building construction requires permission from a local authority when construction remains permissible.
material_facts: The lands were within an area governed by a town-planning scheme that required owners to obtain local-authority permission before constructing buildings.
The restriction was not a complete prohibition, and construction could take place after permission was granted.
issues.conclusion: The lands were not excluded from the definition of vacant land on the ground that local-authority permission was required before construction.
issues.legal_principle: Under section 2(q)(i) of the Urban Land (Ceiling and Regulation) Act, 1976, land is excluded only if construction is not permissible under the applicable building regulations; a requirement to obtain permission is not a total prohibition. The Court agreed with Prabhakar Narhar Pawar v. State of Maharashtra, AIR 1984 Bombay 122, and The State of U.P. v. Radha Raman Agarwal, AIR 1987 Allahabad 272, and rejected the contrary approach in Smt. Shanti Devi v. Competent Authority, AIR 1980 Delhi 106.

predicates.urban_land_ceiling_proceeding: The dispute concerns whether land is vacant land for the purpose of an urban land ceiling proceeding.
predicates.construction_requires_local_permission: The applicable planning restrictions require an owner to obtain local-authority permission before constructing a building.
predicates.construction_remains_permissible: A building may be constructed on the land if the required permission is obtained.

issues.definition: When a ceiling proceeding concerns land on which construction is permissible subject to local-authority permission, the land remains vacant land.

issues.legal_issue: A notification proposing acquisition of land does not by itself remove the land from the definition of vacant land.
material_facts: The State issued an acquisition notification concerning the lands for a public purpose and later declared that they were needed for that purpose.
The owners argued that the notification and the restriction on compensation for certain post-notification improvements meant construction was not permissible.
The applicable acquisition law did not prohibit construction on the notified lands.
issues.conclusion: The acquisition proceedings had no bearing on whether the lands were vacant land for the purposes of the ceiling law.
issues.legal_principle: Section 2(q)(i) of the Urban Land (Ceiling and Regulation) Act, 1976 excludes land only where construction is not permissible under building regulations. Section 24, seventhly, of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894 restricts what may be considered in determining compensation but does not prohibit construction. Section 42 of the ceiling law gives it overriding effect. The Court overruled Smt. Shanti Devi v. Competent Authority, AIR 1980 Delhi 106, and approved Prabhakar Narhar Pawar v. State of Maharashtra, AIR 1984 Bombay 122, and The State of U.P. v. Radha Raman Agarwal, AIR 1987 Allahabad 272.

predicates.urban_land_ceiling_proceeding: The dispute concerns whether land is vacant land for the purpose of an urban land ceiling proceeding.
predicates.land_subject_to_acquisition_notice: A public authority has issued a notice proposing to acquire the land.
predicates.acquisition_notice_does_not_bar_construc: The acquisition notice and applicable acquisition rules do not prohibit construction on the land.

issues.definition: Land subject to a proposed acquisition remains vacant land in a ceiling proceeding when the acquisition notice does not prohibit construction.

issues.legal_issue: Land reserved for public construction remains vacant land when construction is possible by a public authority even if the owner cannot build on it.
material_facts: The town-planning scheme reserved the lands for construction of public staff quarters.
The owners could not themselves construct buildings on the reserved lands, but construction by a public authority was permissible.
issues.conclusion: The reservation did not exclude the lands from the definition of vacant land.
issues.legal_principle: Section 2(q)(i) of the Urban Land (Ceiling and Regulation) Act, 1976 does not require that the owner personally be able to build; land remains vacant land so long as some person or authority may construct a building on it. The Court agreed with Prabhakar Narhar Pawar v. State of Maharashtra, AIR 1984 Bombay 122, and The State of U.P. v. Radha Raman Agarwal, AIR 1987 Allahabad 272.

rule.if: urban_land_ceiling_proceeding and land_reserved_for_public_construction and owner_cannot_build and public_authority_can_build

predicates.urban_land_ceiling_proceeding: The dispute concerns whether land is vacant land for the purpose of an urban land ceiling proceeding.
predicates.land_reserved_for_public_construction: A planning scheme reserves the land for a public construction purpose.
predicates.owner_cannot_build: The owner is not permitted to construct a building on the land.
predicates.public_authority_can_build: A public authority is permitted to construct a building on the land.

issues.definition: Land reserved for public construction remains vacant land when the owner cannot build but a public authority can.

issues.legal_issue: The government cannot be compelled to complete a separate acquisition proceeding when the land is liable to be acquired under the urban land ceiling law.
material_facts: The lands were included in proceedings under the ceiling law as land exceeding the owners’ permitted holdings.
Separate acquisition proceedings for a public purpose had also been initiated concerning the lands.
The ceiling law provided for acquisition of excess land and compensation under its own scheme.
issues.conclusion: It was not proper to compel the government to acquire the lands under the separate acquisition law, and the existence of those proceedings did not affect the ceiling proceedings.
issues.legal_principle: The ceiling law provides for acquisition of excess vacant land and compensation under its own provisions, and section 42 gives that law overriding effect over inconsistent laws. The government may withdraw land from acquisition under section 48 of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894; the Court stated that it would not be proper to compel acquisition under that Act when the land was likely to be acquired under the ceiling law.

predicates.urban_land_ceiling_proceeding: The dispute concerns the application of an urban land ceiling proceeding to land held in excess of the applicable limit.
predicates.excess_land_likely_to_be_acquired_under_: The excess land is likely to be acquired through the ceiling proceeding under its own acquisition and compensation scheme.
predicates.parallel_public_acquisition_proceeding: A separate public-purpose acquisition proceeding has also been initiated concerning the land.

issues.definition: When excess land is likely to be acquired through the ceiling proceeding and a separate public acquisition proceeding is pending, the government need not complete the separate acquisition.
